# `iterator-invalidated-during-loop`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports mutation of a map while an iterator over that map is active.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Structural mutation can invalidate the iterator and make the next iteration
observe stale internal state.

## When it fires

It applies to recognized iterator bindings and invalidating methods on the same
map inside the loop, including mutations proven by a helper function summary. It
also covers `for` loops over `list.items`, `map.keys()` or `map.values()` whose
body appends to, inserts into, or removes from that same container; a mutation
immediately followed by `break` or `return` is allowed.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn run(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, map: *std.AutoHashMap(u32, u32)) !void {
    var it = map.iterator();
    while (it.next()) |entry| {
        try map.put(entry.key_ptr.* + 1, 0);
    }
    _ = allocator;
}
```
